pages.text: Aba and her classmate Pius had won a school science prize: a day aboard a research ship in the Gulf of Guinea, helping to run a robot submarine called an ROV. Dr Sekyi, the chief scientist, gave Aba the controls. ‘The ship is our lifeline,’ she said. ‘The ROV is our eyes.’
sentences: Aba and her classmate Pius had won a school science prize: a day aboard a research ship in the Gulf of Guinea, helping to run a robot submarine called an ROV.
Dr Sekyi, the chief scientist, gave Aba the controls.
‘The ship is our lifeline,’ she said.
‘The ROV is our eyes.’
pages.alt: Two students in life jackets stand in front of a control screen on a ship with a scientist.

pages.text: The ROV slid below the waves. On the screen, the sea was bright blue. At 10 m, the ROV’s red paint turned grey. ‘Red light does not travel far in water,’ said Pius. ‘Blue goes deepest.’
sentences: The ROV slid below the waves.
On the screen, the sea was bright blue.
At 10 m, the ROV’s red paint turned grey.
‘Red light does not travel far in water,’ said Pius.
‘Blue goes deepest.’
pages.alt: A small yellow robot descends in deep blue water with its red markings looking grey.

pages.text: At 200 m, the blue faded. This is the bottom of the sunlight zone. ‘Now the twilight zone,’ read Aba from the chart. ‘From 200 m to 1,000 m, the light is very faint.’ Silvery fish with huge eyes drifted past the lamps.
sentences: At 200 m, the blue faded.
This is the bottom of the sunlight zone.
‘Now the twilight zone,’ read Aba from the chart.
‘From 200 m to 1,000 m, the light is very faint.’ Silvery fish with huge eyes drifted past the lamps.
pages.alt: A robot lamp lights silvery fish with large eyes in dim blue water.

pages.text: At 1,000 m, the screen went black except for the ROV’s lamps. ‘This is the midnight zone, and the water presses on the ROV with about 100 atmospheres more than at the surface,’ said Pius. ‘Pressure rises by about one atmosphere for every 10 m, and 1,000 ÷ 10 is 100.’
sentences: At 1,000 m, the screen went black except for the ROV’s lamps.
‘This is the midnight zone, and the water presses on the ROV with about 100 atmospheres more than at the surface,’ said Pius.
‘Pressure rises by about one atmosphere for every 10 m, and 1,000 ÷ 10 is 100.’
pages.alt: The screen is black except for the circle of the robot’s lamps; a depth gauge shows 1,000 m.

pages.text: Suddenly tiny blue lights flashed across the screen like fireworks. ‘Bioluminescence!’ said Aba. ‘Animals making their own light.’ A jellyfish rippled past, glowing. In the midnight zone, the only light is the light that animals make.
sentences: Suddenly tiny blue lights flashed across the screen like fireworks.
‘Bioluminescence!’ said Aba.
‘Animals making their own light.’ A jellyfish rippled past, glowing.
In the midnight zone, the only light is the light that animals make.
pages.alt: Tiny blue lights flash around a glowing jellyfish in the dark water.

pages.text: Then the picture shook. A current had pushed the ROV sideways and its tether, the cable to the ship, had snagged on a rock. Alarms beeped. ‘Do not pull hard,’ said Dr Sekyi quietly. Aba’s hands were sweating. ‘Think,’ she told herself. She stopped the thrusters, then reversed very gently and waited.
sentences: Then the picture shook.
A current had pushed the ROV sideways and its tether, the cable to the ship, had snagged on a rock.
Alarms beeped.
‘Do not pull hard,’ said Dr Sekyi quietly.
Aba’s hands were sweating.
‘Think,’ she told herself.
She stopped the thrusters, then reversed very gently and waited.
pages.alt: The screen shakes with a red warning light as the robot’s cable catches on a rock.

pages.text: The cable slipped free. The picture steadied. Everyone breathed out. ‘Good flying, and a good decision,’ said Dr Sekyi. ‘You did not panic and you did not push harder.’ Aba checked the clock. ‘We have used our planned time and the current is getting stronger. We should bring it up. A good explorer knows when to stop.’
sentences: The cable slipped free.
The picture steadied.
Everyone breathed out.

‘You did not panic and you did not push harder.’ Aba checked the clock.
‘We have used our planned time and the current is getting stronger.
We should bring it up.
A good explorer knows when to stop.’
pages.alt: The students and scientist watch the screen steady with relief.

pages.text: As the ROV rose, the camera caught one more thing: a see-through, bell-shaped animal pulsing with soft red and blue light. Nobody on board could name it. ‘It might be known, or it might be new,’ said Dr Sekyi. ‘You recorded it well. Now we check.’ Aba wrote in her log: Most of the deep seafloor has still not been mapped in detail. The end.

activities.question: Why did the ROV’s red paint look grey at 10 m?
options: Red light does not travel far in water

activities.prompt: The ROV is passing 200 m. What do you expect the light to be like at 1,000 m?

activities.question: In the midnight zone, where does light come from?
options: Animals that make their own light

activities.question: Why did Aba decide to bring the ROV up?
options: The planned time was used up and the current was getting stronger

activities.prompt: Put the ocean zones in order, from the surface downwards.
Aba’s hands were sweating, but she stayed calm and thought. When have you had to stay calm and think under pressure?

glossary.definition: A remotely operated vehicle: a robot submarine controlled from a ship.
A cable that connects a robot to its ship.
Small propellers that push a robot through water.
